form_hashmap_false_sharing.note: F.32-1γ-v1 baseline (2026-05-25). Two-pool concurrent writers into a shared @form(hashmap, sync = lockfree, cap = 300000). 100k inserts per writer = 200k total. γ-v1 uses cell-level CAS (3-state occupancy) with NO rwlock or mutex — pure atomic ops on slot[0] + memcpy. On this 2-core / cheap-payload bench: γ-v1 is ~1.39x faster than α (serialized) and ~2.54x faster than β2-v2 (striped+rwlock); closes the gap with Go's sync.Mutex map from 1.66x to 1.18x. γ-v1 is fixed-cap (no grow) and remove-less — author sized cap to 1.5x expected entries to keep linear-probe latency bounded. | Re-baselined 2026-06-11: pre-existing drift vs the 05-25 baseline (confirmed ~16.8M on the pre-#125 bus-queue-change binary — this bench has no bus constructs, so the bus-queue change is not on its code path). 2-core false-sharing variance; correctness-driven drift from changes since 05-25, not a perf bug and not from #125.

Verified correct (len=100000, sum=14999850000). The earlier 'O(N^2) by design / slow' framing is obsolete; this now measures O(N) iteration throughput on a working set past L1/L2. Prior value was last measured 2026-05-24.

fn_scratch_work.note: Re-baselined 2026-06-28: 404 us -> 59.5 us (~7x). The non-allocating-fn scratch elision + native-CPU/O3 removed the per-call subregion overhead this bench targets. Hale now ~7.8x faster than Go (was recorded ~1.07x, near-parity). Small bench (~60us) -> tolerance 0.35.

form_hashmap_get.note: Re-baselined 2026-06-28: iters unified to 150k to MATCH the .go/.js/.py variants (was 500k here only — a 3.3x workload mismatch that ALSO dragged the bench into a ~49MB DRAM/cache-bound regime, the source of its old high variance). At 150k the ~14MB table keeps the loop measuring hash + probe cost. With native target-cpu + O3, Hale lookup is ~1.04ms vs Go's 1.10ms (Hale ~1.05x FASTER) — the old '4.8x behind Go' was the workload+regime mismatch, not a real gap.

form_vec_get.note: Re-baselined 2026-06-28: iters unified to 200k to MATCH the .go/.js/.py variants (was 5M here only — a 25x workload mismatch that made the old cross-language ratio meaningless). At 200k the ~1.6MB working set is L2/L3-resident, isolating the per-element read path. With the compiler's bounds-check elimination (for j in 0..v.len() drops the per-read check) plus native target-cpu + O3 defaults, Hale reads at ~14.9us vs Go's bounds-checked 38.8us (~2.6x FASTER than Go). Small-N bench: median jitters ~11-22us run-to-run, hence tolerance 0.5.

form_vec_push.note: Re-baselined 2026-06-28: iters unified to 500k to MATCH the .go/.js/.py variants (was 10M here only — a 20x workload mismatch). 500k pushes through the doubling-grow path ~17 times. Hale 573us vs Go 2.76ms (~4.8x FASTER per push). The earlier 'push is 11x slower than Go' was the workload-size artifact, not a real gap.

locus_instantiation.note: Re-baselined 2026-05-29. The per-arena subregion_lock correctness fix (2026-05-26, cross-pool freelist race) raised this ~91% (1.79->3.94ms). hale 856dc7d's single-thread fast-path recovered most of it (->~2.43ms); the residual is the per-arena mutex init, removable only by a lock-free subregion freelist (deferred follow-up). Measured on the dev box; the prior 1.785ms baseline was faster hardware (pre-mutex control here was ~1.99ms).

loop_overhead.note: Re-baselined 2026-06-28: 12.0 -> 1.59 ms. The native-CPU + O3 codegen defaults autovectorize the XOR reduction to AVX-512 (~0.016 ns/iter, sub-scalar-cycle). This now measures vectorized-reduction throughput, not scalar loop overhead — Hale's backend vectorizes this loop while Go/V8 don't (~12x vs Go). See the bench source comment.
